yolo_subject.title: AI YOLO Subject & Eye Focus (Bird/Animal)
yolo_subject.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Hybrid AI Engine combining YOLOv8 subject detection, Multi-Layer Head/Eye Zone cropping, 4x4 Specular Catchlight Micro-Grid Variance, and 8x8 Local Patch Grid Bokeh Protection. Measures focus exclusively on sharp subject details (eyes, catchlights, beak, face).
yolo_subject.detects: 🎯 Detects: Hybrid AI subject bounding box + 95th percentile eye pupil, catchlight specular reflection, and beak micro-texture focus.
yolo_subject.pros: ✅ Pros: 100% automated AI subject localization with Bokeh Protection. Completely immune to smooth background blur; pin-sharp bird & wildlife eyes/head portraits score exceptionally high.
yolo_subject.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Slightly higher per-photo inference time (~25ms / photo).
yolo_subject.best_for: 💡 Best For: Birding, wildlife action, shallow depth-of-field portraits, off-center subjects, and heavy background bokeh.

bird_subject.title: Bird & Wildlife Subject ROI (Center Focus)
bird_subject.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Crops a central 60% Region of Interest (ROI) box ([y1:y2, x1:x2]) where subjects are centered. Computes a weighted combination of Laplacian variance (60%) and Tenengrad gradient energy (40%) on the crop.
bird_subject.detects: 🎯 Detects: Subject focus in central crop (completely ignoring background bokeh/sky/trees).
bird_subject.pros: ✅ Pros: Perfect for bird & wildlife photography. Prevents beautiful soft background bokeh or detailed trees/foliage from skewing bird focus scoring.
bird_subject.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Assumes subject is positioned within the central 60% region of the frame.
bird_subject.best_for: 💡 Best For: Bird photography, wildlife, sports, and centered subject action shots.

local_var.title: Local Patch Variance (Bokeh Protection)
local_var.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Divides image into a 10x10 grid of local patches. Computes variance per patch and takes the 90th percentile score, ensuring localized subject sharpness is rewarded even if background is blurred.
local_var.detects: 🎯 Detects: Localized patch texture variance vs global defocus blur.
local_var.pros: ✅ Pros: Distinguishes intentional shallow depth-of-field (portrait bokeh) from actual subject blur.
local_var.cons: ⚠️ Cons: May rank uniform background regions lower if subject is small or off-center.
local_var.best_for: 💡 Best For: Shallow depth-of-field portraits, bokeh photos, and macro shots.

fft.title: FFT Frequency Analysis (Motion Blur)
fft.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Transforms image into 2D frequency domain using Fast Fourier Transform. Masks out central low frequencies and calculates the ratio of high-frequency magnitude spectrum energy.
fft.detects: 🎯 Detects: High-frequency spectrum energy ratio (distinguishes motion blur/camera shake from soft focus).
fft.pros: ✅ Pros: Excellent at detecting directional motion blur, hand-shake, and subject movement that edge operators miss.
fft.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Higher computational cost due to 2D Fast Fourier Transforms.
fft.best_for: 💡 Best For: Action shots, handheld low-light photos, and camera shake detection.

brenner.title: Brenner Focus Measure
brenner.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Computes squared intensity differences between pixels separated by a fixed distance d=2: mean((I(x+2,y) - I(x,y)²). Focus accuracy correlates directly with high pixel-to-pixel contrast.
brenner.detects: 🎯 Detects: High-frequency pixel intensity differences & autofocus accuracy.
brenner.pros: ✅ Pros: Extremely fast focus measure algorithm, excellent for detecting autofocus errors.
brenner.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Sensitive to high-frequency image noise or ISO grain in low-light photos.
brenner.best_for: 💡 Best For: Autofocus verification, sharp subject checks, and sports culling.

tenengrad.title: Tenengrad (Sobel Gradient Energy)
tenengrad.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Computes horizontal (Gx) and vertical (Gy) Sobel gradient vectors across the image. Calculates the mean squared gradient magnitude (Gx² + Gy²). Sharp structural edges yield high gradient energy.
tenengrad.detects: 🎯 Detects: Fine edge gradient sharpness, micro-details & high-contrast boundaries.
tenengrad.pros: ✅ Pros: Highly stable mathematical measure, superior for natural photos, macro textures, and less sensitive to high-frequency ISO noise spikes.
tenengrad.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Slightly higher CPU calculation cost than simple Laplacian variance.
tenengrad.best_for: 💡 Best For: Outdoor nature, architecture, macro textures, and scientific imaging.

laplacian.title: Variance of Laplacian (Default / Fast)
laplacian.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Applies a 2D Laplacian operator (∇²I) over the grayscale luminance channel to measure edge second-derivatives. Sharp images contain steep intensity transitions (high variance), while blurry images produce smooth gradients (low variance).
laplacian.detects: 🎯 Detects: General defocus blur & soft edge variance across the whole photo.
laplacian.pros: ✅ Pros: Ultra-fast execution, extremely low CPU memory footprint, ideal for rapid first-pass culling across thousands of photos.
laplacian.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Can mistake flat low-texture scenes (flat sky, plain walls) or intentional background bokeh for blur.
laplacian.best_for: 💡 Best For: General photography, landscape, studio, and rapid batch filtering.

dhash.title: Perceptual Hash (dHash)
dhash.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Downsamples image to 9x8 grayscale, compares adjacent column luminance values to generate a 64-bit binary perceptual hash bit vector, and calculates bitwise XOR Hamming distance between images.
dhash.detects: 🎯 Detects: Near-identical photos, crops, exposure tweaks & burst shots.
dhash.pros: ✅ Pros: Ultra-fast, highly accurate visual similarity comparison across different image formats and exposure tweaks.
dhash.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Might miss extreme subject pose variations in high-speed burst shots.
dhash.thresh_guide: 📊 Threshold Guide: 1-4 bits = Nearly identical. 6-8 bits = Same image with minor edits / wildlife bursts. >12 bits = Different images.
dhash.best_for: 💡 Best For: General duplicate removal, wildlife burst shots, and near-identical photo culling.

md5.title: Exact File Hash (MD5)
md5.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Computes MD5 checksum on the initial file bytes combined with file byte size. Identifies byte-for-byte exact file duplicates.
md5.pros: ✅ Pros: Zero false positives. Instantly finds byte-level copies ('Copy of...', identical exports).
md5.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Misses edited, re-saved, or re-compressed JPEG variations.
md5.thresh_guide: 📊 Threshold Guide: Fixed exact byte match. No slider threshold needed.
md5.best_for: 💡 Best For: Cleaning duplicate file exports and exact backup copies.

burst_time.title: Burst Time Window
burst_time.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Reads EXIF 'date_taken' timestamps (or file creation times) and groups consecutive photos captured within a configurable delta time window T.
burst_time.detects: 🎯 Detects: Rapid-fire camera burst sequences based on EXIF capture timestamp.
burst_time.pros: ✅ Pros: Groups high-speed burst shots regardless of visual pose changes or subject movement.
burst_time.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Requires valid EXIF date/time metadata in image files.
burst_time.thresh_guide: 📊 Threshold Guide: 0.5s - 1.0s = High-speed sports/birds. 2.0s - 3.0s = General burst sequences.
burst_time.best_for: 💡 Best For: Sports, action, and bird flight burst sequences.
